151678.title: Trading posts of the Dutch East India Company (VOC)
151678.creator: workshop of Johannes Vingboons

editorial.note: This series of paintings hanging high in a row here feature various trading posts of the Dutch East India Company (VOC) in Asia. It was a network between which not only products but also enslaved people were transported.

151707.title: The Windmill at Wijk bij Duurstede
151707.creator: Jacob Isaacksz van Ruisdael

editorial.note: The windmill rises up majestically, defying the dark rain clouds and overshadowing the castle and the church of Wijk bij Duurstede. The River Lek flows in the foreground. This painting is world famous, and rightly so.
This painting is a milestone, for never before had a Dutch painter depicted his native flat, watery landscape in such a monumental format. Dusk is falling, and the light is beginning to fade.

152038.title: View of the Golden Bend in the Herengracht
152038.creator: Gerrit Berckheyde

editorial.note: Amsterdam’s huge population growth required it to expand in the 17th century: the city’s rings of canals were dug in phases. This is Herengracht under construction, with some plots still undeveloped.

152048.title: Amsterdam City View with Houses on the Herengracht and the old Haarlemmersluis
152048.creator: Jan van der Heyden

editorial.note: Van der Heyden captured the activity on and around the water in Amsterdam’s old town centre. With an eye for detail, he painted the old Haarlemmersluis, a lock on the Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal.

152296.title: The Grand Canal with the Rialto Bridge and the Fondaco dei Tedeschi
152296.creator: workshop of Canaletto

editorial.note: Studio of Antonio Canale, called Canaletto (1697 - 1768). The Grand Canal with the Rialto Bridge and the Fondaco dei Tedeschi. J.W. Edwin vom Rath bequest, 1941.
This work depicts an imaginary canal. While it is clearly inspired by Amsterdam models, Jan van der Heyden gave it his own twist.

152467.title: The Quay de Paris in Rouen
152467.creator: Johannes Bosboom

editorial.note: During the Romantic era, the picturesque French city of Rouen in Normandy was a popular destination for artists. They were fond of medieval architecture and considered the great cathedrals to be an expression of pure Christian faith.
